content:
Hi,
the following code used to work on v.4.31 but now throws a warning:

-- `Signature`: universes `u`, `v`, `w` only occur together.
-- This usually means there is a `max` expression in
-- the type where none of these universes appear on their own.
--
-- Note: This linter can be disabled with `set_option linter.checkUnivs false`
structure Signature where
    (constants: Type u)
    (vars: Type v)
    (relationSymbols: Type w)
    (relationArity: relationSymbols → Nat)

I don't really get what the problem with this is and how to fix it. I tried telling lean explicitly that the structure should be of type Type ((max u (max v w)) + 2), but this did not help. It's just a warning so not a blocker, but I would still like to understand this.
The checkUnivs linter is new (to core at least), and this looks like a false positive to me. cc @Wojciech Różowski

Thanks for reporting that! Basically, if you look at the type of Signature you get:
Signature.{u, v, w} : Type (max (max (u + 1) (v + 1)) (w + 1))
and indeed in this one u, v, w do not appear on their own.

If you look at its constructor, you get: 

Signature.mk.{u, v, w} (constants : Type u) (vars : Type v) (relationSymbols : Type w)
  (relationArity : relationSymbols → Nat) : Signature

which is fine and each of the mentioned universes appear on their own.

I am wondering, does it mean that we should take information from the constructors into the analysis performed by checkUnivs? As this indeed feels like false positive behaviour to me.

To me it feels like for commands that add multiple declarations, like structure or inductive, the linter should probably take all declarations into account simultaneously and only warn if the universes only occur together in all new declarations.
